title: Grateful Dead Live at Madison Square Garden on 1982-09-21
lineage: Sennheiser 421's (18th row - Center) > Sony TC-D5 > Master Cassette > Playback on Nak Dragon > Sony R700 DAT deck (sbm-on) - used only as A>D converter (44.1khz) > ZA2 > CDR (x1)  > EAC(tracked with Addawav & CDWav) >SHN

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard capture of a high‑energy ’82 show highlighted by the smoking Playin’ > Crazy Fingers opener and standout Touch of Grey/West L.A. performances.
ai_review.review: The recording is praised for its clean, crisp soundboard mix (with only a slight “trashy” drum character) that lets Jerry’s ripping leads and Phil’s thunder‑bass shine through. Musically the show is described as one of the best fall ’82 dates – the opener is fire‑blazing, the set flows smoothly and songs like Touch of Grey, West L.A., Good Lovin’ and Big River are singled out as exceptional.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently high star ratings (average ~4.5) coupled with enthusiastic comments about both performance and soundboard quality; only minor recording quirks noted.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, clean mix praised by multiple reviewers; a few note the drums sound slightly trashy but overall an excellent soundboard capture.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The set is described as flowing naturally from a monster opener through tight jams, with the band “just playing well” throughout.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly noted for ripping leads and perfect tone during the opening jam.
band_member_comments.Phil: His bass is described as thundering through sub‑woofers, adding power to the mix.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bobby’s onstage rap and vocal contributions are highlighted as classic moments.
band_member_comments.Keys: Brent’s funky organ riffs receive specific praise.
band_member_comments.Drums: Generally solid but a few reviewers call the drum sound “a little trashy.”
